title: Graph retrieval, agent memory and source authority
summary: A context window, a retrieval index and durable notes are not the same memory.

claims.text: Microsoft GraphRAG is a particular graph-based retrieval approach. Context engineering includes selective retrieval and persistent notes outside the active context.

levels.overview: Explain what is stored, what is selected now, and what remains authoritative.
levels.architecture: Separate source documents, disposable indexes, graph assertions, session context and durable notes.
levels.detail: Follow an exact returned source and its generation binding. Do not turn a returned result into proof of comprehension.

example.input: A synthetic note references source revision A; source revision B removes its basis.
steps: Retain the old note as dated evidence.
Request a reviewed update rather than rewriting history.
example.output: A stale-note explanation with a source link.
limits: No claim that DataPass Brain uses Microsoft GraphRAG.
Graph structure alone does not establish factual correctness.

alternatives.label: Files and exact lookup
alternatives.whenToConsider: Consider when selected sources are small and well keyed.

alternatives.label: Scoped lexical/graph retrieval
alternatives.whenToConsider: Consider when justified relations and measured retrieval benefit exist.

interview.question: Does adding a graph database give an agent reliable memory?
answerHints: Separate persistence, retrieval, scope, provenance and evaluation.
Explain why the database choice alone cannot establish correctness.

instanceMappingPolicy: An explicit source-pinned link is required; names, icons and tags are not evidence.
